title: Food for Health
seo_title: Food for Health Class 4 EVS Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 5)
standard_code: Class 4, Our Wondrous World Chapter 5: Food for Health
standard_text: Nutrients in food and their work; energy-giving, body-building and protective foods; a balanced diet; millets and seasonal foods; how food spoils and ways of preserving it; healthy eating habits (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 5).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 4 EVS worksheets for NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 5: nutrients, energy-giving, body-building and protective foods, a balanced diet, millets, food spoilage and preservation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A balanced diet keeps us healthy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Food gives us nutrients. Carbohydrates and fats give energy (rice, roti, ghee), proteins build the body (dal, milk, eggs), and vitamins and minerals protect us (spinach, oranges, carrots). Fibre and water are needed too. A balanced diet has all of these in the right amounts; millets such as ragi and jowar are especially nutritious.

Food spoils when germs grow on it. We preserve it with salt and oil (pickles), sugar (jam), drying (papad, raisins), boiling and cold (milk). Eat on time, chew well, wash hands and keep food covered.

Example

Dal is mainly…

it helps us grow

Answer: a body-building food (protein)

Example

Jam is preserved with…

it is very sweet

Answer: sugar

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sweets are energy-giving and therefore healthy in any amount.
  • Eating uncovered food.
  • Skipping breakfast.

items.q: Why do athletes eat more energy-giving foods?

items.e: They also need protein for muscles.

items.q: Which nutrient is mainly needed for giving us energy to work and play?
items.e: Carbohydrates: giving us energy to work and play.

items.q: What do vitamins and minerals mainly do for our body?
